article_title: Really Great Reading's Foundational Literacy Programs
citation: Really Great Reading. (2023). Really Great Reading. https://www.reallygreatreading.com
title: Deliver foundational literacy instruction with existing classroom staff and no additional personnel
description: RGR is designed so that "Classroom teachers, paraprofessionals, or tutors can deliver instruction" and "No additional staff is required." This staffing model keeps implementation feasible within existing school resources, complementing the program's emphasis on efficient instruction and minimized teacher preparation time through digital lesson delivery tools.
requirements: Delivery by classroom teachers, paraprofessionals, or tutors already present in the school
target_learners: Early elementary students receiving Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3 support
target_learning_goals: Foundational reading skills including phonics and fluency
examples: The studied implementation assigned instruction to regular classroom teachers across 13 schools
key_sources: Really Great Reading. (2023). Really Great Reading. https://www.reallygreatreading.com

article_title: Differences in exam performance between pupils attending selective and non-selective schools mirror the genetic differences between them
citation: Smith-Woolley, E., Pingault, J.-B., Selzam, S., Rimfeld, K., Krapohl, E., von Stumm, S., Asbury, K., Dale, P. S., Young, T., Allen, R., Kovas, Y. & Plomin, R. (2018). Differences in exam performance between pupils attending selective and non-selective schools mirror the genetic differences between them. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-018-0019-8
title: Gene-environment correlation (rGE) accounts for genetic differences between school types: selection on heritable traits makes school assignment genetically structured
description: The article offers gene-environment correlation as the explanatory framework for its findings: 'genetic factors are contributing to variation in educational environments'. Children are 'intentionally phenotypically selected, but unintentionally genetically selected' into school types because the traits schools select on—ability, achievement, SES—are heritable. The authors distinguish evocative rGE (being selected on genetically influenced traits) from active rGE (children selecting environments correlating with their genotype), and note that academically gifted children tend to come from academically gifted parents who 'not only provide the genes but also the environments to help them progress academically'.
requirements: A polygenic score for a heritable selection-relevant trait and measures of the selection factors schools use
constraints: The article notes the majority of variation in EduYears GPS occurs within school type, not between types (d = 0.41 implies approximately 83% distribution overlap)
target_learners: Secondary-school students in England transitioning at age 11 across state non-selective, grammar and private school types
target_learning_goals: Educational achievement at age 16 (GCSE composite of English, mathematics and science)
examples: The study found mean EduYears GPS differences between school types that vanished after controlling for heritable selection factors, which the authors interpret as unintentional genetic selection via phenotypic selection
key_sources: Smith-Woolley, E., Pingault, J.-B., Selzam, S., Rimfeld, K., Krapohl, E., von Stumm, S., Asbury, K., Dale, P. S., Young, T., Allen, R., Kovas, Y. & Plomin, R. (2018). Differences in exam performance between pupils attending selective and non-selective schools mirror the genetic differences between them. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-018-0019-8

article_title: Practice and application of blended teaching based on RG-UClass in a preventive medicine course.
citation: Liu Sha, Zhang Jiale, Shang Yuqi, Jiang Yufei, Zhang Xueyan, Hu Zhiyong, Chen Caiyun, Mi Wei. (2026). Practice and application of blended teaching based on RG-UClass in a preventive medicine course. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1885005
title: RG-UClass smart teaching platform
description: RG-UClass (Ruijie-UClass) is an interactive teaching system for university classroom instruction described as "a multi-terminal, full-process integrated tool" that establishes a closed-loop teaching workflow covering online pre-class learning and offline in-class interaction. Built-in functions include attendance tracking, real-time questioning, and case discussions, with automatic grading (objective-item accuracy over 98.7%), lesson reports, and whole-process teaching data capture supporting iterative teaching improvement.
requirements: Requires teachers to build a hierarchical course tree centered on knowledge points and upload chapter materials before class
constraints: The article notes few applications of the RG-UClass hybrid teaching model in teaching practice exist so far
examples: Used to deliver a 54-hour preventive medicine curriculum through pre-class online preview, in-class online/offline combination, and post-class online assignments and discussion
key_sources: Liu Sha, Zhang Jiale, Shang Yuqi, Jiang Yufei, Zhang Xueyan, Hu Zhiyong, Chen Caiyun, Mi Wei. (2026). Practice and application of blended teaching based on RG-UClass in a preventive medicine course. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1885005
